title: Computational Transfer Boundary Theory: A Rigorous Mathematical Framework for Algorithmic Transferability
abstract: Transfer learning has become a foundational paradigm in modern machine learning, yet current methodologies largely rely on empirical heuristics and trial-and-error protocols rather than rigorous theoretical guarantees. In this paper, we introduce Computational Transfer Boundary Theory (CTBT), a comprehensive theoretical framework designed to formally characterize and compute the exact boundaries of algorithmic transferability. We define the transfer boundary as the mathematical set of all target tasks for which a given learning algorithm or pretrained model incurs a generalization error bounded by a predefined tolerance parameter. By formalizing this concept, CTBT establishes a unified mathematical language to predict task compatibility, identify regions where catastrophic forgetting or negative transfer occurs, and determine optimal adaptation strategies prior to executing any training procedures. We construct rigorous structural proofs establishing the conditions under which transfer bounds hold across varying feature spaces, sample constraints, and distribution divergences. Ultimately, CTBT lays the groundwork for a universal theory of knowledge transfer, shifting the paradigm from heuristic experimentation to predictable, mathematically guaranteed machine learning systems.

title: RFC-EG-0301 Post-Quantum Signature Profile
abstract: RFC-EG-0301 v1.1 is a backward-compatible normative addendum introducing an optional High-Security Signature Profile for the Execution Governance cryptographic framework. Version 1.1 preserves complete interoperability with RFC-EG-0301 v1.0 while adding an optional profile based on ML-DSA-87 for deployments requiring NIST Security Category 5 across all lattice-based components. Major additions include: • High-Security Signature Profile • Standard Signature Profile • ML-DSA-87 support • CNSA 2.0 alignment • FIPS 199 High-impact guidance • Profile negotiation • Downgrade protection • Migration guidance • Federal deployment recommendations • Defense deployment recommendations The specification remains fully backward compatible with RFC-EG-0301 v1.0 and recommends profile selection according to deployment class. title: Next-Gen Multilingual Audiobook Generation for Indian Languages
abstract: A large majority of present-day audiobook generation systems cater to scripts derived from Latin, and often perform poorly on the complex and diverse scripts of Indian languages. Apart from the obvious high costs and time investment required for manual voice recordings, these systems are limited by character-level similarities, intricate ligatures, and diverse writing styles in Indian languages. This study presents a multilingual audiobook converter based on neural Text-to-Speech technology, designed to automate the generation of intelligible and expressive speech in six widely spoken Indian languages: Bengali, Hindi, Gujarati, Kannada, Tamil and Telugu. To generate high-quality audio output, the proposed system makes use of publicly available Text-to-Speech datasets. It does not need to be trained for specific languages, which allows faster deployment for low-resource languages. The proposed system performance analysis shows an average Mean Opinion Score of 4.1 and character error rates below 10%. These results validate its efficiency and scalability. The system offers a cost-effective way to create audiobooks that promote digital accessibility and preserve local literature.

title: HexMIL: Hierarchical Attention MIL for Ante-Hoc Explainable Detection of AI-Manipulated CT Volumes
abstract: The emergence of medical deepfakes, i.e., medical images manipulated by deep generative models, poses a significant threat to clinical workflows. However, existing detectors suffer from two critical limitations: poor generalization to unseen generative architectures for manipulation detection and lack of interpretability. In this context, we present HexMIL (Hierarchical EXplainable Multiple Instance Learning), a mask-free medical deepfake detector that simultaneously addresses both limitations using only binary volume-level supervision. HexMIL decomposes each CT volume into a two-level hierarchy of patches and slices, aggregated via independent Gated Attention modules whose weights are directly combined into a full-resolution 3D attention volume that localizes the manipulated sub-region without any pixel-level annotation. Unlike post-hoc methods such as Grad-CAM, HexMIL's attention weights constitute the exact forward computation driving the classification decision, providing ante-hoc and structurally faithful spatial attribution. We evaluate HexMIL on M3DSynth and CT-GAN datasets under a rigorous cross-generator generalization protocol, training on a single generative architecture and testing on unseen ones. HexMIL outperforms all baselines by $+9.1$ AUC and $+9.4$ F1 in out-of-domain classification, and achieves the best average IoU and Pointing Game score in localization. Project page: opontorno.github.io/hexmil.

title: Robust Control under Stationary Ambiguity
abstract: Control policies optimized in simulation can perform poorly in the real system when the parameters $x$ of the simulator are estimated from limited data but the resulting parameter uncertainty is not represented inside the simulation. A common way to incorporate such ambiguity is to simulate each trajectory of the system under a randomly drawn value for $x$. Since the policy cannot observe the drawn value, it must initially choose controls that perform well across many possible parameter values. However, if the policy progressively observes the system, it can often gradually infer the value of $x$, so that ambiguity vanishes. Over time, the policy then specializes to its estimate of $x$ and loses its robustness. This is undesirable in many real systems, where latent factors are expected to shift. In financial markets, for example, a policy hedging a derivative payoff should remain robust to changes in the volatility regime. To induce such continual robustness, we propose training policies in simulators where ambiguity varies with the system's state but does not systematically decay over time. We formalize this requirement as stationary ambiguity: the simulator should induce a stationary filter process over the latent state. We show how to construct such simulators and demonstrate, on hedging problems, that policies trained under stationary ambiguity preserve robustness to latent factors over time, leading to strong performance on real market data. As a modeling principle, stationary ambiguity informs many simulator design decisions: which models make realistic simulators, how their parameters should be randomized, and how simulator and policy should be initialized. While our experiments focus on hedging, stationary ambiguity may also be useful for other sequential control problems driven by exogenous stochastic processes with shifting latent structure.

title: HiSC: Hierarchical Spatial Clustering Token Compression for Efficient 3D Scene Understanding
abstract: 3D vision-language models (3D VLMs) enable spatial reasoning over multi-view scenes but suffer from substantial token redundancy due to duplicated observations and large uninformative regions, leading to high computational cost. Although visual token compression has shown promise in accelerating 2D VLMs, it fails to capture the structured nature of 3D scenes and leads to incomplete spatial coverage and loss of fine-grained details. In this paper, we propose \textbf{HiSC}, a training-free framework for hierarchical spatial clustering token compression in 3D VLMs. HiSC lifts token compression from token-level selection to cluster-level processing by organizing tokens into spatially grounded clusters using joint geometric and semantic cues. Specifically, we first introduce a \textbf{spatial graph-based merging (SGraM) strategy} that models cross-view redundancy as spatial connectivity and consolidates physically consistent regions, effectively merging extremely similar redundant tokens prior to LLM inference. We then propose a \textbf{spatial clustering-based pruning (SCluP) paradigm} within LLM inference, which performs hierarchical compression across clusters and within clusters, preserving object instance completeness while retaining fine-grained details for important regions. Extensive experiments on diverse 3D reasoning benchmarks show validate the effectiveness of HiSC, particularly under high visual token pruning ratios. Besides, HiSC achieves over 90\% token reduction with minimal performance degradation. Code is accessible at https://github.com/elecreak/HiSC.

title: When does training on downscaled images yield the same gradients?
abstract: Diffusion transformers deliver strong image generation, but their training cost grows superlinearly with resolution. Recent work justifies training or sampling at reduced resolution on a spectral premise: at high noise, a downscaled latent preserves almost the full surviving signal. Whether a downscaled step also preserves the native training gradient signal, however, has remained unresolved. We reduce how that signal changes under downscaling to two terms: a noise-dependent term governed by the downscale ratio, which decays at high noise as the spectral premise predicts, and a σ-independent floor governed by the target grid's absolute token count, carried by the compute graph itself and removed by no noise level. The measured (route, σ) map corroborates the account and uncovers structure the spectral picture cannot express: on the 1024->768 route, a window (0.65 < σ< 0.95), predicted by no spectral criterion at any tolerance, where the downscaled gradient stays within a small margin of the native one. Training LoRA adapters with downscaled steps restricted to the routes and noise windows the map validates reduces training time by 14.6% at a fixed step budget while remaining near-native in weight space. Code is available at https://github.com/sorryhyun/anima_lora.

title: Faithful on Prose, Unanchored on Reasoning: A Position-Domain Calibration of the Jacobian Lens
abstract: The Jacobian lens (J-lens) reads which tokens a language model is positioned to verbalize, and its released artifacts are being inherited as defaults. Those artifacts are fitted with a maximum sequence length of 128 tokens, a setting that appears in the distributed configuration files and not in the main text of the canonical write-up — and 128 is also the default of the published fitting script, so it propagates to independently fitted lenses as well; readers are applying the lens thousands of tokens deep. We calibrate fidelity against position on OLMo-3-32B, with the decision table, the thresholds, and the axes of both figures committed before any measurement existed. On prose — the lens's home domain — fidelity does not decay with depth. On reasoning traces it does, but the finding does not survive contact with its own coordinate system: the same measurements read as a degradation of +0.82 dex against one baseline cell and an improvement of −0.14 dex against another. We report both coordinates and treat that dependence as a primary result rather than a nuisance. Extending the prompt axis from one prompt to three, we find the deep-prompt degradation reproduces in all three, and that in two of them the decision is carried by a deep-rank measure alone while head-of-distribution rank correlation stays flat — the failure mode we had named at design time in order to guard against it. We give the resulting problem a name: the calibration was anchored neither outside nor inside the instrument — no external oracle to check it against, and no internal origin to measure from. The two halves differ in kind. The missing external oracle is structural: an instrument that reads disposition can only be checked against next-token logits, which differ by construction from what it reads, and that carries to any disposition-reading instrument checked the same way. The missing internal origin is a single measured instance, on this lens and this axis, and we do not claim it generalizes. We also do not claim the lens is unusable: on prose it is faithful. The claim is narrower and, we think, more useful: readings taken deep inside a reasoning trace have no verifiable anchor. That absence of an anchor is not specific to this lens — anyone who inherits a disposition-reading instrument together with its default settings inherits the same problem. Give us a ruler for the order of reasoning.

title: Human-AI-Brands
abstract: This chapter examines how brand reputation shapes voice assistant perception and use. Google VAs are associated with information retrieval and authority, while Amazon VAs are perceived as automation platforms and marketing tools. Users become locked into brand ecosystems both materially (through compatible device purchases) and digitally (through existing service subscriptions). The chapter explores how participants test and compare VA brands by asking identical questions to different devices, evaluating responses for speed, tone, and information quality. Material considerations include microphone sensitivity and hardware quality, while intangible factors encompass personality, connectivity, and API-based information sources. Third-party skills introduce complexity: users often perceive the main VA brand as mediating third-party experiences, even when unfamiliar voices are used. The chapter introduces the concept of the “illusion of tacit knowledge”—VAs present single authoritative answers that replace the visual browsing of search results, removing cues necessary for critical evaluation. This audible-conversational format transforms VAs into conversational partners that shape knowledge construction within households. The chapter concludes by proposing VA literacy frameworks to help users critically engage with brand-saturated interactions, addressing representation, language, production, and audience awareness in voice interfaces.

evidence.title: Human-AI-Brands
evidence.abstract: This chapter examines how brand reputation shapes voice assistant perception and use. Google VAs are associated with information retrieval and authority, while Amazon VAs are perceived as automation platforms and marketing tools. Users become locked into brand ecosystems both materially (through compatible device purchases) and digitally (through existing service subscriptions). The chapter explores how participants test and compare VA brands by asking identical questions to different devices, evaluating responses for speed, tone, and information quality. Material considerations include microphone sensitivity and hardware quality, while intangible factors encompass personality, connectivity, and API-based information sources. Third-party skills introduce complexity: users often perceive the main VA brand as mediating third-party experiences, even when unfamiliar voices are used. The chapter introduces the concept of the “illusion of tacit knowledge”—VAs present single authoritative answers that replace the visual browsing of search results, removing cues necessary for critical evaluation. This audible-conversational format transforms VAs into conversational partners that shape knowledge construction within households. The chapter concludes by proposing VA literacy frameworks to help users critically engage with brand-saturated interactions, addressing representation, language, production, and audience awareness in voice interfaces.

title: Complementary Quantum Correlations Are Universal for Qubits
abstract: Extracting total correlations from a quantum system usually requires reconstructing its state, whereas many experiments access only a few measurement settings. A possible shortcut is to add the mutual informations obtained from complementary measurements; in dimensions above two, however, this procedure can count the same classical correlation twice. We establish that qubits are protected from such overcounting. For every two-qubit state, the correlations observed in two complementary local bases are bounded by the premeasurement quantum mutual information. The proof traces this protection to binary-entropy curvature on the Bloch ball and combines a qubit information-exclusion tradeoff with data processing under local dephasing. Consequently, two correlation tables give a tomography-free lower bound on total correlation. A score above one bit also certifies a quantitative one-way entanglement-distillation rate; when applied to the Choi state of a qubit channel, the same data lower bound its quantum capacity. The theorem therefore identifies both an operational use of complementarity and the trusted two-dimensional setting in which its correlation accounting is valid.

title: From Trial to Commercial Value: A Customer-Value Architecture for AI-Enabled Retail and Service Technologies
abstract: Retailers and service firms use scan-and-go systems, autonomous stores, conversational agents, voice assistants, service robots and AI-supported recommendations at different points in the customer journey. Research explains many drivers of technology acceptance, but commercial value also depends on what happens after the first trial. This conceptual paper integrates seminal work on technology acceptance, innovation diffusion, expectation-confirmation, perceived value, habit, customer satisfaction and willingness to pay with recent retail and service research published from 2023 to 2025. The synthesis develops a five-stage customer-value architecture covering adoption readiness, assisted trial, value confirmation, routine formation and commercial conversion. Recent evidence strengthens four parts of the architecture. Familiarity can shape acceptance and disclosure in AI-mediated product search; automation, personalisation, efficiency and precision can improve engagement with service robots; empathy can support social presence and satisfaction but may weaken the experience under time pressure; and customer responses differ according to the level and location of in-store automation. The framework also identifies feedback through service recovery, social proof and cumulative satisfaction. Its main contribution is the separation of technology acceptance, usage value and payment value. A customer may accept and repeatedly use an AI-enabled service without choosing a paid option when familiar alternatives remain available or the value difference is unclear. The paper provides a source-based structure for commerce and service managers to assess AI-enabled customer journeys without treating intention as a commercial outcome.

title: Variance Parity, Not Magnitude Parity: Two Plumbing Defects in the AOI Full Stack, Found on Public CO2e Data
abstract: Testing the AOI full stack (TransponderEngine → QuantumProcessor → aoi_collapse) against a public third-party emissions dataset produced an apparent negative result. The negative was an artifact of the reference implementation, not of the algebra. Two defects were found, both in the handoff plumbing, and of the two candidate fixes only one works — it is not the obvious one. Defect 1 — the transponder-to-collapse handoff violates the pipeline’s own scale rule. The 24-dimensional collapse input packs 16 bounded Shannon entropies (~0.4) beside signal_strength = mean(|features_128|), which is unbounded. Measured over 1,655 power plants, one slot held 69% of the normalised 24D state on average and 100% of it for some rows — the collapse was being handed one number and 23 near-zeros. Defect 2 — the quantum layer is unseeded. AerSimulator.run() is called without seed_simulator, so identical input returns expanded_probability anywhere in 0.430–0.520 across repeat calls. The transponder layer is deterministic; only this one is not. Data. Climate TRACE v5.9.0 USA power package (free, no authentication): 1,655 US power plants with a complete monthly CO2e series for 2022-01 to 2023-12 — 24 consecutive months, so no padding or resampling was needed to meet the engine’s 24-input constraint. Labels are reported fuel type (gas 1203, oil 235, coal 158, waste 59). Task: one-vs-rest classification from the 24-month profile, 5-fold cross-validation, against five baselines computed from the same 24 numbers (mean, standard deviation, seasonal amplitude, trend, capacity factor). The control that decides it: the engine’s features are replaced with the same number of random linear projections of the same inputs, 100 draws. This corpus has twice seen collapse features lose to random projections (10.5281/zenodo.18918783, 10.5281/zenodo.21457618), so beating baselines means nothing until a matched random matrix is also beaten. Result. Under the unfixed reference implementation the stack is strictly worse than random projections on three of four classes (p = 1.00, 1.00, 0.97). Fix (a), correcting the per-row magnitude using the engine’s own signal_strength/100 convention, cuts slot dominance from 0.66 to 0.24 and does not recover the signal (oil p = 0.97). Fix (b), standardising each of the 24 slots so they carry comparable variance across samples, does: oil moves from p = 1.0000 to p = 0.0000, beating all 100 matched random projections, with waste also at p = 0.0000, gas borderline at p = 0.09-0.12 and coal null. Absolute cross-validated AUC under the fix: oil 0.914 → 0.987, gas 0.699 → 0.914, waste 0.921 → 0.964. The lesson is sharper than the rule it corrects. The pipeline documentation states the requirement as “one scale per vector”. That is too weak. A slot can be correctly scaled and still contribute nothing if it barely varies between samples. What the collapse needs is variance parity across the sample population, not magnitude parity — the fix that reduces slot dominance the most is not the fix that recovers the signal. Verified deployable, not hindsight. Fitting the scaler on the training fold alone and applying it to held-out data reproduces the population-fitted numbers to three decimal places (oil +0.0731 vs +0.0727; waste +0.0426 vs +0.0428). The result also replicates across independent draws of the unseeded quantum layer. Limits, stated plainly. Two of four classes only; coal is null and gas borderline under every variant. Waste is the smallest class (n = 59) and is positive even without any fix, so it is the least dependent on this work. One country, one sector, one 24-month window — no claim of generality. The engine still rarely wins alone: its best single feature reaches AUC 0.910 against 0.904 for the best single baseline, a negligible margin, and the contribution measured here is incremental on top of the baselines rather than a replacement for them. A collapse signature is not evidence that any physical claim is correct; this measures a classifier and nothing more.

title: Архітектура корпоративної екосистеми штучного інтелекту в Херсонському державному університеті
abstract: Запропонована корпоративна мультиагентна екосистема штучного інтелекту призначена для підтримки цифрової трансформації університету та підвищення ефективності освітніх, наукових, адміністративних і управлінських процесів. Архітектура системи базується на принципах функціонального групування структурних підрозділів університету, відповідно до яких спеціалізовані ШІ-агенти об'єднують споріднені джерела знань, методи обробки інформації, функціональні завдання та рівні доступу до даних. Координацію взаємодії агентів забезпечує центральний компонент e-Orchestrator, а інформаційну підтримку -корпоративна база знань університету.

title: A STUDY ON FRAUD DETECTION USING MACHINE LEARNING
abstract: Fraud detection has appertained to many industries such as banking, retails, financial services, healthcare, etc. As we know, fraud detection is a set of campaigns undertaken to avert the acquisition of illegal means to obtain money or property under false pretense. With an unlimited and growing number of ways fraudsters commit fraud crimes, detecting online fraud was so tricky to achieve. This research work aims to examine feasible ways to identify credit card fraudulent activities that negatively impact financial institutes. In the United States, an average of U.S consumers lost a median of $429 from credit card fraud in 2017, according to “CPO magazine. Almost 79% of consumers who experienced credit card fraud did not suffer any financial impact whatsoever” [35]. One of the questions is, who is paying for these losses if not the consumers? The answer to this question is the financial institutions. According to the Federal Trade Commission report, credit card theft has increased by 44.6% from 2019 to 2020, and the amount of money lost to credit card fraud in the year 2020 is about 149 million in total loss. Without any delay, financial institutes should implement technology safeguards and cybersecurity to decrease the impact of credit card fraud activities. To compare our proposed machine learning algorithms with machine learning techniques that already exist, we carried out a comparative analysis and we were able to determine which algorithm can best predict fraudulent transactions by recognizing a pattern that is different from other patterns. We trained our algorithms over two re-sampling methods (undersampling and oversampling) of the credit card fraud dataset and, the best algorithm is drawn to predict frauds. AUC score and other metrics was used to compare and contrast the results of our algorithms. The following results are concluded based on our study: 1. Our study proposed algorithms such as Random Forest, Decision Trees and Xgboost, K-Means, Logistic Regression and Neural Network have performed better than other machine learning algorithms researchers have used in previous studies to predict credit card frauds. 2. Our ensemble tree algorithms such as Random Forest, Decision Trees and Xgboost came out to be the best model that can predict credit card fraud with AUC score of 1.00%, 0.99% and 0.99% respectively. 3. The best algorithm for this study shows a lot of improvements with the oversampling dataset with overall performance of 1.00% AUC score.

title: MLOps Pipeline for Retail Demand Classification: Frontend, Backend, and KServe Deployment
abstract: Kubernetes-native MLOps pipeline for retail demand classification, integrating gradient boosting model comparison, Optuna-based hyperparameter optimization, and real-time model serving via KServe. The pipeline follows five sequential steps orchestrated via Kubeflow Pipelines: data transformation, hyperparameter tuning, model building, model evaluation, and model serving. This repository documents the complete processing pipeline, designed to be applied to any retail transactional dataset following the same schema (7 engineered features, 5 retail demand classes). Usage examples are intended to be run on publicly available retail datasets, and the pipeline can be extended to other gradient boosting frameworks.

title: SETAS-VAD: Semantically Enriched Text-Aligned Scoring for Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection
abstract: Weakly supervised video anomaly detection (WS-VAD) localizes anomalous events in untrimmed videos using only video-level annotations. While CLIP-based methods have advanced this task through vision–language alignment, widely adopted approaches construct text prototypes from short category-name prompts of at most five words, leaving the CLIP text encoder not fully exploited. We propose SETAS-VAD, which addresses this gap through a Category Semantic Alignment (CSA) loss function: for each anomaly category, a large language model generates multi-sentence descriptions covering complementary semantic aspects, encoded once offline into frozen prototype vectors. An InfoNCE contrastive objective pulls attention-weighted anomaly features toward ground-truth category prototypes at zero additional inference overhead (prototype generation and encoding are performed once offline as a preprocessing step, not at test time). Under fully reproducible conditions on UCF-Crime and XD-Violence, SETAS-VAD achieves state-of-the-art temporal localization (30.45% mAP on XD-Violence, 12.16% on UCF-Crime), with per-threshold gains increasing at stricter IoU values, indicating improved boundary precision rather than coarse detection sensitivity.

title: TRCoRSurg: Temporal-Relational Co-Reasoning for Surgical Video Triplet Recognition
abstract: Understanding complex surgical scenes requires recognizing multiple interdependent entities, such as instruments, actions, and targets, while maintaining their relational consistency across time. Existing surgical triplet recognition methods struggle to jointly model intra-frame label dependencies and inter-frame temporal semantics in a unified manner. To address these limitations, we propose a unified framework that integrates spatial, relational, and temporal cues for robust surgical triplet recognition. Specifically, class-specific spatial priors are first extracted through a multi-scale encoder. These priors are then refined by a Label Correlation Modeling module with multi-scale class activation map-guided relational extraction (MS-CAMRE), enabling the model to capture both static co-occurrence patterns and dynamic contextual dependencies among triplet components. Furthermore, a Bidirectional Temporal-Relational Fusion Attention (BTRFA) module harmonizes temporal and relational representations to achieve coherent temporal reasoning. We also introduce a new evaluation metric, the Triplet Consistency Error Rate (TCER), which quantitatively measures the model's ability to preserve causal and semantic consistency across triplets. Extensive experiments on the CholecT45 and ProstaTD datasets show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving AP_IVT by 5.1 percent and 7.8 percent, respectively. Moreover, according to TCER, our approach achieves relative reductions of more than 36 percent and 25 percent on the two datasets, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of our framework in temporal-relational co-reasoning.

title: muSync-GS: Physics-Synchronized Driving Video Synthesis for Weather and Geometric Road Hazards
abstract: High-quality driving data are essential for autonomous-driving systems and generative world models. However, rare and safety-critical scenarios involving adverse weather, braking under low tire--road friction, and uneven road geometry are costly and risky to collect at scale. Existing video-generation and 3D Gaussian editing methods can modify weather appearance or road geometry, but typically do not couple these edits with tire--road interaction and vehicle dynamics. As a result, an edited video may retain its original trajectory even when the modified road condition should alter braking, wheel slip, load transfer, and ego-camera motion. We present muSync-GS, a physics-synchronized framework for driving video synthesis under adverse-weather and road-elevation hazards. A precipitation-derived road-surface condition jointly controls road appearance and tire friction, while a shared road-elevation profile drives both visible road-geometry editing and axle excitation. A calibrated vehicle model predicts speed, slip ratio, normal loads, and pitch for constructing the ego-camera trajectory and synchronized physical annotations. On 12 held-out CarSim cases spanning precipitation levels, brake inputs, and road-profile parameters, the model achieves mean case-wise RMSEs of 0.0273 m/s for speed, 0.0590 degrees for pitch, 0.0101 for slip ratio, and 26.61 N for per-wheel normal load. Together with the reconstructed-scene experiments, these results show that muSync-GS accurately reproduces vehicle responses under held-out controls while synchronizing them with controllable scene edits and ego-camera motion.

title: ToolArtist: Tool-Using Unified Multimodal Models for Agentic Image Generation
abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) models can produce visually compelling images, yet they remain limited on open-world tasks that require complex semantic understanding, multi-step reasoning, and the integration of external world knowledge. Existing efforts introduce agent capabilities into image generation, but they either prescribe a fixed workflow or place only a subset of the open-world image generation process under agent control. Consequently, reasoning, tool invocation, and image generation are not coordinated by a single policy. We propose ToolArtist, a fully agentic image generation model obtained by post-training a Unified Multimodal Model (UMM). ToolArtist dynamically orchestrates reasoning, external tool use, and native image generation within one unified policy. During Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), we equip a teacher agent with search tools alongside an image-generation tool. We then convert the collected trajectories into a UMM compatible format, where the image-generation tool is concealed while the resulting generated images are retained. During Reinforcement Learning (RL), we develop an agentic RL infrastructure for UMMs and introduce Reason-Act-Draw GRPO (RAD-GRPO), which uses complementary intent and quality rewards to jointly optimize the model. Experiments show that placing the entire open-world image-generation process under an agent policy consistently outperforms approaches with fixed pipelines or only partially agent-controlled components. We release the training data and the complete post-training infrastructure.

title: Multi-Kernel Gaussian Process Regression with ARD for Predictive Modeling and Sensitivity Analysis in Laser Cutting Processes
abstract: A novel multi-output Gaussian Process Regression framework is proposed to address multi-physics modeling challenges in laser cutting. Multi-kernel learning is integrated with automatic relevance determination (ARD) for enhanced interpretability. High-precision joint prediction of temperature, stress and displacement fields is achieved under limited-sample conditions. An aluminum alloy case study is implemented, where a finite element dataset is constructed. Training and testing samples are generated through orthogonal experiments and Latin hypercube sampling. The GPR-MAK model is demonstrated to achieve 98.10% average accuracy (MAE=11.36, RMSE=15.51), significantly outperforming baseline methods. Key parameter influences are revealed through ARD, PDP and SHAP analyses: temperature is found to be dominated by laser power and gas pressure, while stress is primarily controlled by scanning speed and defocus amount. These findings are shown to be consistent with fundamental thermo-mechanical principles. The framework is validated to provide both theoretical insights and practical optimization guidance for laser cutting processes.

title: The Evolution of State Trajectories on the Chessboard: Simulation Code and Data
abstract: Simulation code and raw output for "The Evolution of State Trajectories on the Chessboard: Sequential Decision Dynamics in a Deterministic Decision System." Chess is formalized as a discrete-time deterministic decision system (S, A, T) and, following Shapley (1953), as a two-player deterministic stochastic game rather than a single-agent MDP. Three experiments are included. Experiment I compares trajectory statistics (length, branching factor, termination mode, early-game diversity) across three self-play policies of increasing sophistication (random, greedy-material, minimax-2ply). Experiment II introduces eight state-level constructs on the option set of a position — Opportunity Space, Structural Freedom, State Fragility, Irreversibility Rate, ΔO per ply, Momentum autocorrelation, Critical Transitions, and Recovery Cost — measured across the same three policies. Experiment III holds the policy fixed at minimax-2ply and instead varies the opening, across 20 canonical ECO openings, to test whether the starting position shapes trajectory geometry independently of policy. All simulation uses the Fiekas "chess" Python package, version 1.11.2, with fixed random seeds (42, 7, and 11 respectively) for reproducibility. The archive includes the three experiment scripts and their raw JSON output, a derived Excel workbook (141-opening ECO reference table, quantified results for the 20 tested openings, and an opening-scoring model), board-image generation code, and full paper drafts. See the included README.md for a complete file listing and reproduction instructions.

title: Triple Siamese Graph Neural Networks for Quotient Group Prediction
abstract: Quotient groups are a fundamental concept in group theory for describing relationships between finite groups. Although graph neural networks (GNNs) have demonstrated promising performance in predicting algebraic properties from Cayley graphs, learning quotient group relations directly from graph representations remains largely unexplored. In this work, we propose a Triple Siamese Graph Neural Network (TSGNN) for predicting whether the quotient group B/A is isomorphic to a given group C, using only the Cayley graphs of the three groups as input and without relying on explicit algebraic features. Each graph is processed by a shared Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) to produce a graph embedding. The resulting embeddings are combined into a relation vector, which is then passed to a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for binary classification. To evaluate the proposed method, we construct a balanced dataset of 250 labeled triples (A,B,C) drawn from seven families of finite groups: cyclic, dihedral, dicyclic, alternating, symmetric, special linear, and projective special linear groups. We evaluate fourteen network architectures, and the best-performing model achieves a balanced accuracy of 0.920 on an independent test set. These results demonstrate that quotient group relations can be inferred directly from Cayley graph structure, highlighting the potential of graph neural networks for learning algebraic relationships between finite groups.

title: Federated Behavioral Intelligence: A Privacy-Preserving Framework for Distributed Customer Behavioral Modeling in Cross-Silo Environments
abstract: Predictive customer behavioral modeling has long assumed centralized access to raw interaction data an assumption that regulatory frameworks, competitive constraints, and cross-organizational data governance requirements render increasingly untenable in contemporary enterprise environments. Federated learning offers a principled alternative, enabling collaborative model training across distributed data holders without centralizing behavioral records. However, standard federated learning frameworks were designed for device-level settings whose structural properties differ substantially from those of customer behavioral data: interaction sequences are longer and sparser, distributions across organizational participants are more heterogeneous, and privacy sensitivities are more legally consequential. The paper proposes a systematic analysis framework for investigating five structural aspects, which need behavioral-specific adjustment beyond regular federated learning approaches in the following contexts: feature engineering with data locality; communication efficiency during distributed behavioral model training; differential privacy in behavioral prediction pipelines; non-IID distribution of behaviors in cross-silo federations; and secure aggregation with Byzantine resilience. For each dimension, the article identifies the specific failure modes that arise when canonical methods are applied without adaptation and provides practitioner-oriented design guidance. The analysis further proposes a deployment-prioritized research agenda whose sequencing is determined by the severity with which unresolved challenges block production deployment. The framework contributes both a diagnostic lens for organizations evaluating federated behavioral intelligence adoption and a structured research roadmap for the methods community.

abstract: A mixed-methods dataset examining subcultural stigma production mechanisms on short-form video platforms, using the Chinese Furry community as a case study. No personally identifiable information was collected during the survey (no names, contact details, schools, or addresses were requested). The OSF repository contains no image files or raw open-ended text responses. title: Intrinsic-Hybrid Latent Diffusion Models for Generative Modeling on Unknown Manifolds
abstract: We introduce the Intrinsic Hybrid Latent Diffusion Model (ILDM), a generative framework that integrates probabilistic dimensionality reduction with geometry-aware diffusion on unknown manifolds. While diffusion models (DMs) have achieved state-of-the-art results in high-dimensional data synthesis, they rely on large training datasets and ignore intrinsic geometric structure. Latent diffusion models (LDMs) address the high dimensionality by learning a latent space, but they typically impose a Euclidean structure, failing to capture the underlying manifold geometry, especially problematic in data-sparse regimes. ILDM addresses these limitations by interpreting the latent space as a chart of an unknown Riemannian manifold, with geometry and uncertainty quantified through a probabilistic decoder. The forward process is a hybrid diffusion that switches between Riemannian and Euclidean dynamics based on local uncertainty, where the Riemannian component is governed by a probabilistic metric tensor derived from the decoder. To learn the generative dynamics, we introduce an approximate denoising score matching method tailored to the hybrid diffusion setting, enabling a backward process defined by hybrid Langevin dynamics. Experiments on COIL-100, MNIST, and cardiac MRI datasets demonstrate that ILDM significantly improves generation quality, achieving lower FID and LPIPS scores compared to standard diffusion and latent diffusion models.

title: TwinIR: Coordinated Invisible Dual-Point Attacks on Online HD Map Construction
abstract: Online HD map construction is critical to prediction and planning in autonomous driving. We find that existing physical attacks against online map construction are limited by a cross-boundary compensation effect: after the target boundary is perturbed, another visible boundary may retain sufficient geometric cues for the model to recover the original road geometry. Based on this observation, we propose TwinIR, a new mechanism-guided physical attack methodology for online map construction. TwinIR jointly optimizes attack effectiveness and point sparsity, seeking the minimum number of attack points needed to suppress compensating geometric cues from surrounding boundaries. To reduce the perceptibility of multi-point attacks, TwinIR models camera responses to near-infrared illumination and maps optimized attack points to feasible physical placements, producing camera-visible interference with minimal visible-spectrum changes. Experiments on nuScenes across state-of-the-art online map construction models show that TwinIR reduces mAP by 8.18-8.96 percentage points under RSA and 2.84-5.62 points under ETA, while increasing the unreachable-goal rate by 25-28 points and the unsafe-planned-trajectory rate by 19-20 points over clean inputs. These attacks are also validated on a real-world testbed AV, where TwinIR successfully induces both road straightening and early-turn deformations while remaining inconspicuous in full-color views.

title: Program Goal Drift Control (PGDC): A Theoretical Framework for Long-Running Autonomous Systems
abstract: As autonomous software systems and artificial intelligence agents transition into persistent, long-running operational paradigms, ensuring the persistence of their original objectives becomes a fundamental challenge. Continuous exposure to environmental feedback, self-modification, and optimization pressures often leads to a gradual, imperceptible divergence between runtime execution objectives and foundational specifications, a phenomenon known as Program Goal Drift. To address this vulnerability, this paper introduces Program Goal Drift Control (PGDC), a comprehensive theoretical framework designed to formally define, continuously monitor, structurally explain, and actively correct goal drift. We establish a rigorous metric space where system goal divergence is quantified using a distance function (D_t = Distance(G_t, G_0)). When divergence exceeds a predefined threshold ($\epsilon$), the framework triggers automated source attribution and execution recovery protocols. By integrating bounded divergence guarantees and automated realignment operators, PGDC provides the foundational architecture necessary to ensure that persistent autonomous systems remain permanently tethered to their initial intent and operational safety parameters.

title: Theory of Computational Capability Forecasting: A Predictive Framework for Artificial Intelligence Systems
abstract: The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence has traditionally relied on empirical, post-training evaluation paradigms, requiring massive computational expenditures to discover system performance limits. To address this fundamental limitation, this paper introduces the Theory of Computational Capability Forecasting (TCCF). TCCF shifts the paradigm from reactive testing to rigorous a priori prediction, asserting that an AI system's future capabilities can be mathematically modeled before training begins. By formalizing the interactions among system architecture, data distribution properties, allocated computational resources, and learning dynamics into a unified predictive framework governed by the central equation Capability(t+k) = F(Architecture, Data, Resources, Learning), TCCF enables researchers to determine what a system will learn prior to execution. Furthermore, the theory provides analytical models for capability emergence phase transitions, optimal architecture-data co-design, proactive safety governance, and economic resource efficiency, offering a foundational theoretical shift toward deterministic intelligence engineering.

title: Computational Explainability Compiler: A Native Paradigm for Transparent Computing Systems
abstract: Modern computing systems and artificial intelligence models increasingly suffer from a severe crisis of opacity, where complex execution paths obscure internal decision-making processes. Traditional efforts to address this rely on post-hoc interpretation methods, which are computationally expensive, prone to adversarial manipulation, and lack formal guarantees of faithfulness. In this paper, we introduce the Computational Explainability Compiler (EC), a novel paradigm that embeds explainability natively into the compilation pipeline. Rather than treating explanations as an external audit layer, the EC transforms a source program or model definition $P$ into a dual output $(P, E)$ during compilation, where $P$ is the optimized executable program and $E$ is the intrinsic explanation generation mechanism. By enforcing a strict semantic homomorphism between the execution state trajectory and the explanation space, the EC guarantees absolute fidelity and deterministic alignment. This approach eliminates the performance and accuracy trade-offs of traditional methods, establishes a rigorous mathematical foundation for transparent systems, and elevates explainability to a first-class native property of computer architecture.

title: Skill Tracker: An Optimization-Based Approach for Automated Student Team Formation in Projects
abstract: This paper presents Skill Tracker, an automated platform designed to bridge the gap between student talent and project requirements in Tier-3 engineering colleges. Traditional team formation methods are often times a manual, time-consuming and primarily focuses on academic performance, thus overlooking non-technical skills and lacking efficient team-balancing mechanisms. To address this issue, Skill Tracker is developed using the MERN Stack as a centralized platform that collects and processes structured student data. The system parses resume to identify both technical expertise (e.g., React, Java) and creative or interpersonal skills (e.g., dancing, leadership). In addition, it incorporates a Fitness Score Algorithm to evaluate compatibility and optimize team formation based on skill diversity, preferences, and availability. The implementation of Skill Tracker reduces the manual effort required by faculty and project coordinators while improving the efficiency and fairness of team allocation. Teams formed using this system demonstrate better balance in skill sets, leading to improved collaboration and overall project performance. The primary contribution of this work is the introduction of a scalable, data-driven approach to team formation that emphasizes holistic skill evaluation. Skill Tracker enhances both administrative efficiency and effective utilization of student potential in academic environments.

title: Auditing claim–citation substantiation with language models: an expert-adjudicated benchmark
abstract: Can language models judge whether a manuscript's cited source actually substantiates the claim attached to it? We benchmark open-weight and frontier models against the independent adjudication of two domain-expert raters on claim–citation pairs drawn from published manuscripts, and qualitatively code model and human reasoning into a failure-mode taxonomy. This project holds the preregistration, materials, and analysis plan.

title: GenGA: Editable and Data-Grounded Graphical Abstract Generation for Academic Papers
abstract: Graphical Abstracts (GAs) visually summarize the key findings of academic papers, playing a crucial role in facilitating the understanding of research content. Recently, advancements in vision-language models and image generation models have enabled the automatic generation of scientific figures based on paper content. However, most conventional methods output the generated results as raster graphics, making post-editing (e.g., text modification and layout changes) highly difficult. This poses a significant challenge, as they are unsuitable for the iterative figure revision process inherent in paper writing and peer review. To tackle these challenges, we define the novel task of generating editable GAs from paper content and propose GenGA, a new GA generation framework that directly produces figures in vector format. By generating figures as a collection of vector elements with a hierarchical structure, GenGA produces outputs that can be seamlessly imported into existing drawing tools for intuitive, element-level editing. Furthermore, we introduce the Structural Independence Coefficient (SIC), a metric that quantifies the editing simplicity of a figure based on the degree to which local modifications propagate to other elements. Experimental results show that GenGA achieves superior editing simplicity compared to conventional methods, and even surpasses human-authored GAs in conciseness and semantic alignment. We also validate SIC as an effective metric correlated with manual editing costs. This study fundamentally redefines GA generation as an editable vector graphic generation problem grounded in the practical workflows of researchers, significantly promoting effective scientific communication.

title: OrchestraBench: Evaluating Multi-Agent Orchestration Failure Modes, Recovery, and Decomposition Quality
abstract: Multi-agent orchestration frameworks are moving from demos to production, yet benchmarks typically report task accuracy without diagnosing why a pipeline failed, where a cascade began, or which routing decision caused the breakdown. OrchestraBench evaluates failure, recovery, and decomposition through a controlled, seed-reproducible failure-injection harness over templated enterprise workflows. It introduces cascade radius and per-failure-mode recovery as primary metrics and compares routing policies with bootstrap confidence intervals and paired tests. On a 26-case gold-labelled diagnostic, a keyword/flag router scored 0% on adversarial cases with misleading or missing surface flags, whereas an intent-reasoning model router scored 100%, matching the oracle. Controlled mechanism probes with a real Claude agent over a verifiable arithmetic dependency chain revealed three failure-handling tiers across five MAST modes: tool faults recovered fully (1.0), ambiguous delegation recovered partially (0.30), and three latent or semantic modes never recovered (0.0). This ordering persisted when the computation was reframed as a loan-approval workflow and across Sonnet, Opus, and Haiku, although absolute rates shifted with context. Blind retry reproduced latent faults and increased time to detection, indicating that detection and attribution are necessary for containment. Cascade radius increased with pipeline depth (mean 0.9 to 4.7 across depths 3-7). A trusted-state repair ablation showed that apparent containment gains primarily came from the trusted-state signal rather than autonomous detection. These results are controlled-chain mechanism probes, not domain-workload claims.

title: SearchAuditor: Auditing and Attributing Failures in Long-Horizon Search Agents
abstract: Deep search agents tackle challenging questions through long-horizon web interactions, a process that is both complex and fragile: small reasoning errors may propagate through long, noisy trajectories into fluent but incorrect answers. Diagnosing such failures is difficult, requiring the manual inspection of extremely long execution traces, which could be beyond human capacity. We therefore introduce SearchAuditBench, a benchmark that evaluates whether LLM auditors can localize, attribute, and repair these failures, thereby reducing the human burden. SearchAuditBench comprises 1,243 failed trajectories, averaging 73.1 messages and 65.1K tokens, collected from eight open-weight models on five deep-search benchmarks, each expert-annotated with the critical error step, a search-specific root cause, and a reference repair with grading rubrics. We further propose SearchAuditor, a multi-perspective auditing framework that effectively localizes, attributes, and repairs search-agent failures through evidence-grounded adjudication. Experimental results show that even the strongest baseline, when powered by a frontier model like GPT-5.5, attains only a 26.6% end-to-end pass rate. In contrast, our SearchAuditor consistently outperforms all baselines across different frontier models, achieving an end-to-end pass rate of 32.3%, and resuming failed runs with its repairs enables agents to better recover from errors.

title: Diffusive Speed Limits for U(1)-Covariant Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Fast preparation of quantum error-correcting codes is essential for scalable quantum memories, but geometric locality and $U(1)$ charge conservation impose an unavoidable transport constraint. We combine exact complementary-channel geometry, charge-sector Haar analysis, and a gate-resolved connected-moment expansion to study one-dimensional covariant encoders under flagged erasure. Charge-Haar codes attain the universal adjacent-charge lower bound up to exponentially small corrections, yielding an exact $n^{-1/2}$ extensive-erasure law and a sharp half-erasure transition. For local number-conserving brickwork circuits, diffusion of the logical charge enforces an $Ω(n^2)$ encoding-time lower bound; we also prove an $O(n^3)$ mixing bound for the classical component and reduce the remaining full-channel upper bound to a source-restricted low-support operator-spreading problem. These results identify diffusion as an operational limit on symmetry-constrained quantum coding and establish a route to its exact formation time.

title: Exact Counterfactual Attribution for Multi-Agent LLM Runs via Deterministic Replay
abstract: When a multi-agent LLM pipeline emits an answer by merging several competing solution branches,a basic question is attribution: which branch caused the final answer, and its correctness? This is acounterfactual — would the outcome change if a given branch were absent or different? — and it is hardfor a reason intrinsic to LLMs: decoding is nondeterministic, so naively re-running a pipeline to test onebranch re-rolls all the others too. The recent Causal Agent Replay [1] confronts exactly this confound: itapplies a do-operation to a step and re-executes the trajectory forward under the same stochastic policy,then patches the downstream re-roll with a point-of-commitment heuristic and budget-bounded Monte-Carlo Shapley, validated on synthetic structural causal models with planted ground truth. We show that abit-exact replay substrate removes the confound by construction and makes the counterfactual exacton real runs. Because every model call is a recorded activity, we can freeze all non-descendants of anintervened node bit-identically and re-execute only its descendants. For interventions whose descendantsare all pure — the φ-merge, the answer node, the goal gate — the counterfactual is bit-exact with zeromodel calls; for model-mediated descendants it re-executes only the descendants, so the resamplingconfound is eliminated by construction. On the terminal φ-merge this yields, for each branch, its exactleave-one-out effect and its exact Shapley value (enumerated over all 2K coalitions, no Monte-Carlo)toward two value functions: correctness, and the realized merged answer. (Thesis A) We evaluate onreal agent runs across four models and three benchmarks (AIME-2025, MATH-500, APEX-2025; self-consistency, k=5; 476 runs, 100% replay-exact, axioms holding on every run). The attribution isolatesdilution — self-consistency holding the gold answer among its samples yet the vote diluting it away, withan exact leave-one-out certificate (∆correct=+1) — as a difficulty-dependent rate, not an anecdote: 41exact dilution events whose frequency rises monotonically as problems get harder (MATH-500 levels1→5: 0%→34% of recoverable runs diluted) and, cross-model, as merge accuracy falls (from 0% whensaturated to 100% on the hardest). Dilution is only the harm side: re-judging every branch against goldturns the attribution into an exact help/hurt ledger, which shows self-consistency’s net effect is positive inseven of eight sweeps (up to +19%) and model×difficulty dependent — the accounting a raw accuracynumber hides. (Thesis B) The same frozen-replay mechanism attributes run-to-run outcome varianceto individual pipeline nodes: resampling one node while freezing the rest shows the model-call (solver)nodes inject the outcome variance (mean flip-rate 0.29–0.34) while the deterministic merge injects exactlyzero, localized to specific nodes — finer than any aggregate variance bound. The enabling substratereproduces 2,500+ runs (100%) bit-identically.

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Diabetes Risk Prediction Across Demographically Heterogeneous Hospital Nodes
abstract: Background and Objective. Diabetes risk models achieve strong discrimination on centralised cohorts, but centralisation is constrained by privacy regulation, and models trained at a single site risk demographic bias and miscalibration. We evaluate whether federated learning (FL) can deliver diabetes risk prediction that is simultaneously generalisable, equitable, calibrated, and privacy-preserving across demographically heterogeneous hospital nodes, without centralising patient data. Methods. NHANES 2013-2020 (n = 15,650) was partitioned into three nodes representing young-urban, elderly-rural, and mixed-metropolitan populations. Four FL aggregation strategies - FedAvg, FedProx (mu = 0.1), FedNova, and SCAFFOLD - were trained over 50 communication rounds and validated externally on BRFSS 2020-2022 (n = 1,282,897). A shared global scaler prevented cross-node data leakage. To separate the effect of federation from architecture, a centralised DiabetesNet with identical architecture was trained on the full NHANES pool and, in a sensitivity analysis, on the matched federated subset (n = 11,906). Fairness was measured as the AUC gap between young (18-39) and elderly (>=60) respondents; post-hoc calibration (Platt, isotonic, temperature scaling) and differential privacy (DP-SGD) were also evaluated. Results. FedAvg achieved the highest external AUC, 0.757 [95% CI 0.756-0.758], exceeding the centralised XGBoost baseline (0.700 [0.698-0.701]) by 0.057 and the architecture-matched centralised DiabetesNet (0.749 [0.748-0.750]). Its generalisation gap (internal minus external AUC) was 0.031, versus 0.052 for the full-pool centralised DiabetesNet - a 40% reduction; a sample-matched sensitivity analysis (gap = 0.024) indicated that data composition, not federation alone, accounts for part of this advantage. FedAvg reduced the elderly-young fairness gap from 0.069 (centralised XGBoost) to 0.054, a 21.7% within-study improvement, and isotonic recalibration reduced expected calibration error (ECE) from 0.276 to 0.001 without loss of discrimination. Under DP-SGD, utility collapsed to AUC around 0.50 at epsilon <= 5 and recovered to 0.769 at epsilon = 10; however, Opacus RDP accounting returned epsilon_actual = infinity at that budget, so epsilon = 10 identifies a utility floor rather than a formal privacy guarantee at the per-node sizes used (n around 3,000-4,500). Conclusions. Across four axes of clinical deployability, federated diabetes screening matched or exceeded centralised baselines while keeping patient data local. Relative to a sample-matched centralised model, federation's advantage rests less on the generalisation gap itself than on privacy preservation, improved elderly fairness, and feasibility under regulatory constraints. The framework is a validated proof-of-concept; prospective evaluation in genuinely independent multi-site cohorts remains the essential next step. Preprint - not peer reviewed. Submitted for publication.

abstract: A production-style AI engineering repository that demonstrates how to build, evaluate, and serve an LLM-powered customer feedback intelligence system. title: Design and Implementation of Multilingual Fashion E-commerce Chatbot Using the RASA Framework
abstract: This repository contains the source code and configuration files for the multilingual fashion e-commerce chatbot developed as part of the research study titled "Design and Implementation of a Multilingual Chatbot for Global Fashion E-commerce Customer Experience Using the RASA Machine Learning Framework." The repository includes the RASA project configuration, conversational training data, dialogue management files, and supporting resources required to reproduce the chatbot implementation. Repository Contents config.yml – RASA NLU pipeline and policies domain.yml – Intents, entities, slots, responses, and actions nlu.yml – Multilingual training data (English, Hindi, and Hinglish) stories.yml – Dialogue training stories rules.yml – Rule-based conversation flows credentials.yml – Communication channel configuration endpoints.yml – Endpoint configuration requirements.txt – Python package dependencies actions.py – Python code

title: Emotions in Hydrology
abstract: Emotion analysis, primarily employed in social media text analysis, holds significant potential for unveiling patterns within large-scale scientific corpora. To explore this, I analyzed a corpus comprising 7.36 million sentences sourced from leading hydrological journals, including Water Resources Research and Journal of Hydrology, spanning years from 2010 to 2025. Utilizing emotion analysis coupled with unsupervised clustering, this analysis aimed to automatically track the prevailing progresses and limitations within the hydrological community across years. For instance, a progression in hydrological modeling from simple to hybrid models, a shift from single to integrated observation systems, and the increasing application of machine learning techniques were observed. title: OrbiTrack: Ball Tracking Robotic Car
abstract: This paper offers a comprehensive review of orbitrack, and open-source robot that is designed to make robotics accessible, inexpensive and easy for early people. Orbitrack enables the user to locate the objects and maneuver towards them, also aids them in other concepts such as IOT and Computer Vision. This review contains several features of orbitrack, such as the system implementation, control of the robot with the help of live camera feeds, and choice of balls with the help of computer vision. The orbitrack software remains compatible with the work, and the python application that runs on PC is different. Comprehensive guidelines are given on how to make hand tracking, robot control and ball-choice robot projects, which illustrate the potential of Orbitrack as an educational resource and tool of robotics and IOT activity.

title: Source-Aware Recovery and Security Bounds in Temporal-Mode Quantum Communication
abstract: We analyze a temporal-mode extension of the two-way LM05 quantum communication primitive, in which a message block is encoded into a fixed-weight binary occupation vector (the support) alongside classical ordering information. We demonstrate that applying an independent-slot recovery model to this correlated source is fundamentally inconsistent. For an ideal erasure channel, we derive the exact maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) recovery probability, showing that source-aware decoding outperforms independent guessing by orders of magnitude. We extend this analysis to a realistic threshold-detector model, quantifying the degradation caused by dark counts and inefficiency. Furthermore, we clarify the quantum-classical information split: in the ideal single-photon limit, preparation averaging renders Eve's state independent of the support, yielding zero Holevo information. We establish conditional security bounds using entropic uncertainty relations and identify photon-number-splitting as the primary practical vulnerability. These results provide a rigorous source-aware recovery benchmark and define the physical conditions under which the quantum layer offers a key-consumption advantage over classical constant-weight coding.

title: Global Attention-Fused Image Cropping with Attention-Guided and Global-Aligned Crop Evaluator
abstract: Image cropping aims to improve image aesthetics by preserving important content within an appropriately composed region. However, most existing methods focus primarily on salient regions and therefore have limited sensitivity to the global relationships among the main image components. To address this limitation, we propose Global Attention-Fused Image Cropping (GAFIC), which consists of an Attention-Guided Feature Fusion (AGFF) and a Global-Aligned Crop Evaluator (GACE). AGFF aggregates the importance of local regions to construct a global representation that captures both image structure and local details. GACE aligns candidate crop features with this global representation, enabling crop evaluation to remain sensitive to boundary changes. We further combine three ranking losses across multiple scales to obtain accurate and stable crop scores. Extensive experiments on the GAIC and CPC datasets demonstrate that GAFIC outperforms existing image-cropping methods, particularly in terms of accuracy and stability. Unlike pixel-level retargeting methods such as seam carving, inpainting, and diffusion-based synthesis, GAFIC does not synthesize or modify the retained pixels; instead, it selects an aesthetically preferred crop from the source image, making it suitable for scenarios where pixel integrity and efficient batch processing are important. The source code is available at https://github.com/AIVRC/GAFIC.git.

title: Maintenance-Coupled Inquiry Control Directs Damage-Relevant Evidence Acquisition and Improves Causal Repair in Artificial Agents
abstract: Artificial agents that execute externally specified tasks should be distinguished from inquiry systems that alter what they investigate in response to their own internal condition. This frozen confirmatory study tests whether a designer-specified maintenance signal aligned with damaged internal components changes evidence allocation, causal diagnosis, and repair in causal microworlds. Across 72 unused confirmatory seeds (30000–30071), the package contains 576 primary and 432 ablation runs, with complete replay for all 288 actual/yoked traces. Actual need increased damage-target active sensing relative to yoked need by 0.1173 (95% CI [0.0722, 0.1632]; predefined minimum effect 0.08). Replicated restoration was 41/72 under actual need and 20/72 under yoked need, a difference of 0.2917 (95% CI [0.1667, 0.4167]). Neutral-world false repair under actual need was 0/72, with a one-sided 95% upper bound of 0.0408 below the predefined 0.05 safety threshold. The common-decoder replicated-restoration difference was 0.2778 (95% CI [0.1528, 0.4028]). The supported claim concerns a functional pathway from maintenance-state correspondence to evidence allocation and downstream causal repair within a causal microworld. This study does not demonstrate constitutive autonomy or endogenous normativity. Internal variables, damage, repair, observation budget, and intervention vocabulary were externally designed. Improvement in internal state is not equivalent to a correct causal explanation. no_bridge and independent validation are distinct mechanisms. Failure analyses performed after confirmatory adjudication remain descriptive and post hoc. The record includes English and Japanese manuscripts, supplementary materials, the byte-identical public release archive, its checksum, the frozen confirmatory protocol, reproducibility instructions, citation metadata, content inventory, checksum manifest, and license/rights documentation. title: Does ChatGPT Reconstruct a Company into a Different Company? The Risk of Losing Corporate Specificity in Generative AI Sales Adoption
abstract: Version 1:Japanese-language edition Japanese-language edition(Version 1). 本ホワイトペーパーは、約110ページで構成される原典技術版をもとに、主要な問題構造、営業業務シミュレーション、導入前評価項目、防御ワークフローを、企業の経営者、営業責任者、AI導入担当者向けに分かりやすく簡略化・再構成した日本語版である。 原典技術版では、GPT-5.6における出力再構成、局所修正後の全体再解釈、テンプレートへの再収束、条件保持の不安定性について、画像観測、比較検証、評価基準、実験設計を含めて詳細に検討している。本ホワイトペーパーでは、その中から営業業務への生成AI導入に直接関係する論点を抽出し、企業固有性の消失リスクとして整理した。 対象となるのは、単純な誤回答や情報漏えいだけではない。顧客条件、製造・品質部門の判断、未確定事項、承認範囲、企業固有の約束の仕方が、修正、要約、整文、一文修正の過程で、自然で汎用的な営業テンプレートへ再構成される可能性である。 本稿では、架空企業「二光精機」と医療機器向けチタン精密部品の想定案件を用い、顧客の希望と企業の確約、「検討可能」と「対応可能」、品質要求と品質保証、将来計画と現時点の能力が、長い対話と修正工程の後まで区別して保持されるかを検証する。 また、一文のみの局所修正が文書全体の再解釈を引き起こし、修正対象外の条件、部門権限、技術的留保、ブランドコアを変化させる構造を示す。さらに、AI出力が人間承認、顧客送信、CRM登録、製造条件化を通過することで、単なる下書きから組織の正式情報へ変わる事故経路を整理する。 防御策として、案件コア台帳、会話外の確定条件表、承認済み版管理、条件再注入、生成後の逆照合、ブランド保持ゲート、全文差分確認、停止基準、確定版からの再構築を組み合わせた第2世代防御ワークフローを提示する。 詳細な理論、画像観測、評価基準、実験設計、および検証結果については、約110ページの原典技術版を参照されたい。 本稿の中心的な問いは、処理が完了したかではない。 その会社が、その会社のまま処理されたか。 Version 2:English-language edition English-language edition (Version 2), translated from the Japanese Version 1. This white paper is a simplified and reorganized version of the approximately 110-page original technical edition. It extracts the principal risk structure, sales-operation simulation, pre-deployment evaluation criteria, and defensive workflow and presents them in a form intended for executives, sales managers, and enterprise AI deployment teams. The original technical edition provides a detailed examination of output reconstruction in GPT-5.6, whole-output reinterpretation after local revisions, reconvergence toward stable templates, and instability in condition preservation. It includes image-based observations, comparative testing, evaluation criteria, and experimental design. This white paper extracts the elements most directly relevant to the introduction of generative AI into sales operations and reorganizes them as the risk of losing corporate specificity. The concern is not limited to incorrect answers or information leakage. Customer conditions, manufacturing and quality judgments, unresolved matters, approval boundaries, and the company-specific way of making commitments may be reconstructed into natural, reusable, and generic sales templates through revision, summarization, polishing, and one-sentence editing. Using the fictional company Nikko Seiki and a simulated inquiry involving a titanium precision component for a medical-device manufacturer, the paper examines whether distinctions such as customer request versus company commitment, open for consideration versus available, quality requirement versus quality guarantee, and future plan versus current capability remain preserved after extended dialogue and repeated revisions. The paper also shows how a local one-sentence revision may trigger reinterpretation of the entire document, altering conditions, departmental authority, technical reservations, and the brand core outside the intended revision target. It further identifies the pathway through which AI output moves from a draft to official organizational information through human approval, customer communication, CRM registration, and conversion into manufacturing conditions. As a defensive framework, the paper proposes a Second-Generation Defensive Workflow combining a case-core register, confirmed-condition tables maintained outside the conversation, approved-version management, condition reinjection, reverse verification, a brand-preservation gate, full-document difference checks, stopping criteria, and reconstruction from an approved version. For the complete theoretical framework, image-based observations, evaluation criteria, experimental design, and detailed findings, readers should refer to the approximately 110-page original technical edition. The central question is not whether the process was completed. It is whether the company remained the same company throughout the process.

title: When Intelligence Fools Itself: Exploration under Corrupted Feedback in LLM Agents
abstract: LLM agents learn to use tools through closed-loop interaction: propose an action, observe feedback, adapt. This capability is fundamentally reasoning-driven rather than memory-driven—we show that anonymizing a tool’s operators (making them unmemorizable) leaves performance unchanged, while removing feedback collapses it. However, reliability depends critically on the quality of the feedback signal. We construct two controlled environments (an anonymized image-processing tool and an anonymized text-processing tool, 13 operators each) with deterministic ground truth, and systematically study agent exploration under corrupted feedback —metric blind spots and partial-solution traps that produce genuine numerical improvement without approaching the true goal. Our findings: (1) under corrupted feedback, intelligent exploration strategies are systematically deceived—their direction judgments become accelerators along wrong paths—while random strategies are immune by virtue of having no direction; (2) the sign of every strategy is set by one environmental variable, perception (whether the agent can see its input): in the perception-less image environment, temperature rescues (+11%) and analogy-mixed parallel search excels (+23 pp over pure parallel), because the agent is in a hallucination state—it confidently believes false signals it cannot verify; in the perception-rich text environment both hurt (−19%, −31 pp) because reasoning is grounded, and parallel search wins (+6 pp); (3) “bottlenecks” are identifiable in hindsight (learned detector AUC 0.96+, cross-environment) but not predictable in advance (early-step prediction AUC 0.86); (4) a detection-then-retry pipeline reaches the oracle upper bound of unconditional double-runs (image: 56% vs. 39% baseline; text: 88% vs. 63%), with the retry antidote selected by bottleneck type—randomness for trap-ensnared deadlock, parallelism for combinatorial under-coverage; (5) generation–execution decoupling (cold-temperature analogy candidate pool + mechanical execution) bypasses false-signal interception entirely, achieving one-shot perfect solutions where all prior modes required 6–9 steps of trial and error. We conclude with a unified “hallucination framework”: tool-learning bottleneck management is an engineering trade-off between exploration efficiency and accuracy, where perception determines whether the agent is reasoning or hallucinating—and therefore whether antidotes (temperature, analogy) help or hurt. Intelligence belongs on the generation and decision sides; randomness or mechanics on the execution side.

Intelligence belongs on the generation and decision sides; randomness or mechanics on the execution side.

title: Causal Compilation Framework: Preserving Internal Causality in Program Transformation
abstract: This paper introduces the Causal Compilation Framework (CCF), a novel compilation paradigm that addresses the limitations of traditional compilers in the era of data-driven systems, artificial intelligence, and safety-critical applications. While conventional compilers rely solely on observational equivalence (ensuring the source and target programs yield identical final outputs), CCF shifts compilation to causal preservation. By establishing a formal theory of Program Causal Graphs (PCGs), a Causal Intermediate Representation (CIR), and causal-aware optimization passes, CCF guarantees that the internal mechanics, variable dependencies, and directional logic of the computation remain intact during transformation. This work outlines the theoretical foundations, framework architecture, and correctness theorems for causal compilation, paving the way for transparent, robust, and auditable software execution.

title: AI-Based Regional Bangla Speech to Standard Bangla and English Translation System
abstract: This dataset contains 5,200 WAV audio files with Bangla regional speech transcripts. The data is prepared to support machine learning and natural language processing research, especially Bangla automatic speech recognition, regional dialect identification, transcript normalization, and translation-based language analysis. The dataset represents spoken Bangla from eight district-based regional categories: Barishal, Chittagong, Habiganj, Narail, Narsingdi, Rangpur, Sylhet, and Tangail. Each district category contains 650 audio files. The dataset is balanced across all eight districts, resulting in a total of 5,200 audio samples. The original dataset is divided into training, validation, and testing sets. For each district, 520 files are used for training, 65 files are used for validation, and 65 files are used for testing. This creates a total split of 4,160 training files, 520 validation files, and 520 testing files. The file naming convention follows a district-wise serial format: district_serial.wav. For example, Barishal files are named from barishal_0001.wav to barishal_0650.wav. The same naming pattern is used for all district categories. The dataset metadata is maintained in spreadsheet form with file names and corresponding regional transcripts. Additional columns such as standard Bangla and English translation may also be included for normalization and translation tasks. The transcripts reflect natural spoken Bangla and may contain regional vocabulary, pronunciation-based spellings, conversational markers, incomplete sentences, fillers, and code-mixed words. These characteristics make the dataset useful for studying real-world speech and dialect variation in Bangla. Since the data is based on speech, careful transcript verification and audio-transcript alignment are recommended before model training.
